Login (admin/Admin@123) → /dashboard → /scanner; updated copy verified: label 'Barcode / Catalog Code / Cat No / Name', placeholder 'Scan or type code, cat no, or name…', and helper text mentions code/cat no/catalog name. TEST1 catalog_name exact 'MACK' → POST /api/scans 200 → toast 'Found: MACK' → navigates to /catalogs/6a354ab73387987768032286. TEST2 cat_no '9085' → 200 → /catalogs/6a354ab73387987768032343 (HANGER / RSC-00191). TEST3 fuzzy 'INFINITY' → POST returns 409 → multi-match-dialog opens with EXACTLY 2 options [match-pick-RSC-00001 'INFINITY SHEERS I' Available, match-pick-RSC-00007 'INFINITY II' Available]; clicking the first triggers a retry POST with RSC-00001 (200) and navigates to /catalogs/<id>. TEST7 Issue Batch mode: action-select switched to 'Issue Batch' (batch-issue-card visible, basket-count '0 items'), type 'INFINITY' submit → 409 → dialog opens → click first pick → dialog closes, retry POST 200, basket-count becomes '1 item' showing 'INFINITY SHEERS I / RSC-00001', toast '+ INFINITY SHEERS I', user remains on /scanner (no navigation). Visual confirmation in screenshot.
critical_code_review_comments: Scanner.jsx handleMultiMatch() correctly inspects err.response.status===409 AND Array.isArray(detail.matches) before opening the picker — defensive and good. setMultiMatch({value, matches}) preserves the original input so the dialog can show the search string back to the user (good UX).

pickMatch(m) calls setMultiMatch(null) BEFORE await addToBasket(m.catalog_code). This is correct ordering so the dialog closes immediately on click. However if the retry POST itself returns 409 again (it shouldn't because catalog_code is exact), the user would briefly see a closed dialog then re-open — consider guarding pickMatch with a loading flag to disable the buttons during in-flight retry to prevent double-clicks.
Dialog uses sane data-testid IDs: 'multi-match-dialog' on DialogContent and 'match-pick-<catalog_code>' per row — easy to test, good convention.

The 409 response shows in browser console as a red 'Failed to load resource: 409' — this is just axios surfacing the HTTP status; the app handles it cleanly. Consider intercepting in lib/api.js to suppress the console.error for expected 409 multi-match responses, otherwise users opening DevTools may think something is broken.

When 'INFINITY' multi-match dialog is open and user closes via X / Escape (onOpenChange→setMultiMatch(null)), no toast is shown — fine for dismiss-by-choice, but in Issue Batch mode the user might lose context that nothing was added. Optional: add a small 'Cancelled' info toast on dismiss.

Backend lookup tiers (exact codes → name exact → fuzzy contains) is well-aligned with the 3 inputs (code/cat-no/name). cat_no '9085' resolved correctly; suggest backend also documents in OpenAPI the 409 response schema with the matches[] shape so future API consumers know to expect multi-match.

USB hotkey listener already exempts data-testid='scanner-input'; multi-match dialog buttons are <button> elements (not text inputs) so the global keydown listener will swallow keystrokes — confirm via real USB scanner test that scanning a second code while the dialog is open behaves sensibly (current behavior: it would fire addToBasket again and likely open another dialog). Not a blocker but worth a design note.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Scanner cat_no + catalog_name + multi-match picker feature is fully working. Real selectors verified: scanner-input (placeholder mentions code/cat no/name), scanner-submit-btn, scanner-action-select, multi-match-dialog, match-pick-<catalog_code>, batch-issue-card, basket-count. Backend /api/scans returns 200 on exact/single-match, 409 with {detail:{message,matches:[{id,catalog_code,catalog_name,cat_no,status}]}} on multi-name/fuzzy ambiguity, and 404 with detail.message='No catalog matched ...' on no match. The Search/View/Issue Single/Issue Batch action modes all share the same handleMultiMatch path so the picker works uniformly. NOTE for future iterations: keyboard hotkey listener stays armed while dialog is open — if a USB scanner fires while picker is up, it will call addToBasket again; consider gating the global listener on `!multiMatch` if user reports double-scans during disambiguation.
rca_of_the_issue: Feature request, not a bug. Original scanner supported only barcode_value/catalog_code/qr_value. User asked for cat_no and name lookup. Implementation adds 3-tier lookup on backend (exact codes → name exact case-insensitive → contains-fuzzy) plus a 409 multi-match contract; frontend handleMultiMatch surfaces a Dialog with per-match buttons that retry the scan with the exact catalog_code. All seed test cases (MACK exact-name, 9085 cat_no, INFINITY fuzzy→2 matches, NONEXISTENT 404, RSC-00001 regression, USB hotkey, Issue Batch flow) verified end-to-end through the production preview URL.
